FIELD REFERENCE

Turbot fish: Scophthalmus maximus and the Turbot War

Turbot is the flatfish Scophthalmus maximus. The fish called turbot in the 1995 Canada–Spain Turbot War was a different species: Greenland halibut, Reinhardtius hippoglossoides. Check the scientific name before comparing fishery advice. A Canadian reference to turbot does not necessarily describe the European fish on this page.

Updated 2026-11-20 · Castward

Is turbot the same fish as Greenland halibut?

What should you know about turbot?

What was the Turbot War?

It was a 1995 fishing dispute involving Canada, Spain and the European Union. Carleton University describes the seizure of the Spanish trawler Estai on March 9 and an agreement on April 16.

Which fish was involved in the Turbot War?

Greenland halibut, Reinhardtius hippoglossoides. Canadian fishery sources also call this fish turbot.

Is European turbot a halibut?

No. Scophthalmus maximus and Reinhardtius hippoglossoides are different species.

How can I tell their body shapes apart?

FAO describes turbot as nearly circular, with both eyes on the left side. Fisheries and Oceans Canada describes Greenland halibut as diamond-shaped and right-eyed.

Why does an older source say Psetta maxima?

The FAO cultured-species profile uses Psetta maxima for turbot. Compare the common name and description as well as the scientific name when reading older sources.
